rounds.text: Sanghvi Movers Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 15.3x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 8.54x against a sector benchmark of 10.54x [E11]. The business demonstrates powerful fundamental momentum, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 37% [E14] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 57% [E17]. This outpaces the broader sector medians, while profitability metrics like ROCE at 14.79% [E10] and ROE at 14.54% [E9] comfortably exceed sector benchmarks of 6.96% [E10] and 5.46% [E9] respectively. Furthermore, cash generation remains robust with a cash conversion ratio of 1.51x and operating cash flow of Rs 278 Cr in March 2026, ensuring that reported profits are fully backed by cash [E29, E30]. A discounted cash flow model suggests significant intrinsic undervaluation, supported by a reverse DCF indicating that the current price merely prices in 5.0% earnings growth compared to an 18.0% base case [E40, E42]. Conceded: operating margins have decreased over the last four years and free cash flow was negative at Rs -130 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E31].

Sanghvi Movers Ltd carries substantial margin compression risks, evidenced by operating margins dropping significantly from 56% to 35% in TTM, and further declining to 31% in Sep 2026 compared to 38% in the year-ago quarter [E25, E26]. This negative trend in yearly operating margins has persisted over the last four years [E27]. Concurrently, aggressive expansion is draining liquidity, as reflected by a negative free cash flow of Rs -130 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31] and a massive 544.4% surge in capital-work-in-progress to Rs 58 Cr by Sep 2026 [E35]. To fund this capex build-up, borrowings have escalated to Rs 805 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 674 Cr a year prior [E34]. Furthermore, the market is signaling clear lack of momentum, with a lagging relative-strength rating of 19 against the Nifty 500 [E46], a twelve-month price return of -6.3% [E47], and a three-year compounded share price growth of -1% [E22]. Conceded: [E40].

While the bear highlights a contraction in operating margins [E25, E26, E27], this overlooks the company's superior top-line expansion, with 5-year compounded sales growth at 37% [E14], 3-year sales growth at 33% [E15], and TTM sales growth at 30% [E16], easily outpacing the sector median sales growth of 13.5% [E66]. Conceded: the negative free cash flow of Rs -130 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31] and rising borrowings to Rs 805 Cr [E34], but this liquidity deployment is directly reflected in the massive +544.4% build-up in capital-work-in-progress [E35], signaling an active growth phase rather than structural distress. The concern over lagging price momentum and a relative strength rating of 19 [E46] ignores that fundamentals are actively outpacing the stock price [E51], with a 5-year profit growth of 57% heavily eclipsing the 29% share price growth [E21, E51]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current market price implies a modest 5.0% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E42], meaning pessimism is already heavily priced in while operational results continue to show positive money flow [E39] and a good upcoming quarter expectation [E54].

Conceded: 5-year compounded sales growth is 37% [E14] and TTM sales growth is 30% [E16]. However, this top-line expansion has failed to protect profitability, as operating margins have severely compressed from 56% three years ago down to 35% in the TTM [E25], accompanied by a yearly operating-margin trend that reads decreasing over the last four years [E27]. The bull's dismissal of negative free cash flow of Rs -130 Cr [E31] and rising borrowings to Rs 805 Cr [E35] as a benign growth phase ignores that this aggressive capital deployment coincides with decelerating earnings growth [E61] and an inconsistent quarterly margin trend [E28]. While the bull points to a low reverse DCF expectation [E42], the market price accurately reflects very real execution risks, including a laggard relative strength rating of just 19 against the Nifty 500 [E46], a 12-month price return of -6.3% [E47], and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown reaching -88.3% [E48].
